sentences.text: The petitioners, who claim to be the owners in possession of the land, detailed in Para-2 of the petition, have claimed the reliefs of directing the respondents to pass the final award in terms of Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in the Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 as the proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act initiated after issuance of Notice under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act stand lapsed because the final award has not been passed and directing the respondents to release compensation in favour of the petitioners as per the market rate.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
02. According to the petitioners, on the indent placed by respondent No. 3, Collector,
Reasi/respondent No. 2 issued notice under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act and thereafter the Deputy Commissioner, Reasi requested on 03.04.2012 vide communication No.Col/LA/ADC/RSI /12/346-50 to issue declaration under Sections 6 & 7 of the Land Acquisition Act and the Deputy Commissioner, Reasi requested the Divisional Commissioner, Jammu for issuance of such declaration as the amount of compensation exceeded the jurisdiction of the Deputy Commissioner.

03. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the notification under Sections 6 & 7 and 9 &
9(A) of the Act were issued and thereafter though objections were filed by them but the same were not considered and the possession of the land was taken over by the respondents.
He further submits that the possession of the land was taken over in 2013 and the draft award was issued on 02.07.2013 along with the apportionment statement of the village Bhangal.

Despite the draft award prepared, final award has not been passed till date nor the payment has been made, therefore,
according to the petitioners, proceedings have lapsed.
They, therefore, claim compensation under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in the Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 04. The main grievance of the petitioners, on which this claim is made, is that the proceedings have lapsed with the efflux of time as the final award has not been made, for which claim of compensation is made within the time prescribed in the Act.

05. Respondent No. 2/Collector has filed his objections and stated in para-4 of the objections that the said road has now been notified as National High way (NH-144) and Competent Authority for Land acquisition (Deputy Commissioner) Reasi has made a communication to the Principal Secretary to the Government, PWD (R&B) Department, Civil Secretariat, J&K for taking up the matter with Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) for placement of indent in the case of acquisition of land under National Highways Act, 1956 vide communication No.
DCR/RSI/SQ/22-23/7218-21 dated 05.12.2022.
06.

entities.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
So the reply of the Collector makes it clear that fresh acquisition proceedings are to be initiated,
for which the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has been approached for placing indent for acquisition of the land in question under the National Highways Act, 1956.
07.

entities.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Since the respondents themselves stated that the fresh indent is to be placed for acquisition of the land so that the land in question is acquired under the National Highways Act, 1956.

Having regard to this relief claimed by the petitioners as has been rendered infructuous, the respondents having stated that no road has been notified as National High way (NH-144) and Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has been approached for placement of indent, the respondents to initiate the proceedings according to the Act, for acquisition of the land.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners, who claim to be the owners in possession of the land, detailed in Para-2 of the petition, have claimed the reliefs of directing the respondents to pass the final award in terms of Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in the Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 as the proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act initiated after issuance of Notice under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act stand lapsed because the final award has not been passed and directing the respondents to release compensation in favour of the petitioners as per the market rate.
02. According to the petitioners, on the indent placed by respondent No. 3, Collector,
Reasi/respondent No. 2 issued notice under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act and thereafter the Deputy Commissioner, Reasi requested on 03.04.2012 vide communication No.Col/LA/ADC/RSI /12/346-50 to issue declaration under Sections 6 & 7 of the Land Acquisition Act and the Deputy Commissioner, Reasi requested the Divisional Commissioner, Jammu for issuance of such declaration as the amount of compensation exceeded the jurisdiction of the Deputy Commissioner.
Despite the draft award prepared, final award has not been passed till date nor the payment has been made, therefore,
according to the petitioners, proceedings have lapsed.
They, therefore, claim compensation under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in the Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
Since the respondents themselves stated that the fresh indent is to be placed for acquisition of the land so that the land in question is acquired under the National Highways Act, 1956.
Since the project has been notified as National Highway, therefore,
fresh proceedings are required to be initiated for acquisition of the land.
opennyai_summary.decision:
08. Having regard to this relief claimed by the petitioners as has been rendered infructuous, the respondents having stated that no road has been notified as National High way (NH-144) and Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has been approached for placement of indent, the respondents to initiate the proceedings according to the Act, for acquisition of the land.
They shall proceed expeditiously preferably within a period of six weeks from the date copy of this order is made available to the respondents/authorities concerned.
09. Disposed of in the above terms.
